active_runtime.reason: The active readback manifest publishes exact file hashes, sizes, source roles and authority paths, while the current isolated execution environment has neither target-PC access nor a published downloadable 5.10.2.3.7 source package ID. Findings that require exact active main.js/workspace.js line inspection are therefore marked AUTHORITY_LEVEL or A6_RUNTIME_PROBE_REQUIRED, not falsely presented as direct byte-level findings.

findings.title: PER_ROLE_HIDDEN_BROWSERWINDOW_LIFECYCLE_IS_BOUNDED_BUT_RESOURCE_HEAVY

evidence.fact: cRoleWindows and cRoleDispatchTails are keyed Maps.
releaseCModeRoleWindow deletes the Map entry and destroys the BrowserWindow.
ensureCModeRoleWindow reuses a live role window or creates one hidden BrowserWindow; backgroundThrottling is false; window-open is denied; closed and render-process-gone delete the Map entry.
The runtime calls releaseRole at stop, commander/worker report, carryover, repeat-command and pause/delete transitions.

findings.assessment: The source contains explicit close/destroy cleanup and reuse, so a leak is not proven statically. The immediate performance risk is simultaneous hidden BrowserWindow count multiplied by active roles while background throttling is disabled. Release timing depends on external GitHub/report state transitions, so delayed or missing reports can retain high-cost hidden renderers longer than intended.
findings.immediate_target: A6 must measure BrowserWindow/webContents/process/RSS/CPU at 1, 5 and 10 simultaneous roles and after each release transition. Candidate optimization should enable background throttling when idle or suspend/throttle hidden role windows outside active dispatch/verification windows.
findings.later_target: Replace per-role persistent BrowserWindow retention with a bounded pool only if A6 proves material resource savings without losing per-role session correctness.

findings.title: RENDERER_HAS_EVENT_DRIVEN_RENDER_PLUS_MUTATION_OBSERVER_PLUS_UNTRACKED_5_SECOND_REFRESH

evidence.fact: scheduleRender coalesces UI work through requestAnimationFrame.
C-mode and repeat-command events schedule render or refresh.
boot creates a subtree MutationObserver and starts setInterval(refresh, 5000); neither handle is stored for teardown.

findings.assessment: requestAnimationFrame prevents same-frame duplicate render, but the renderer still has three independent update triggers. The 5-second interval runs while idle and has no visibility or teardown policy. A duplicated boot or fragment reinjection would create another interval, observer and event subscription.
findings.immediate_target: Store interval/observer/subscription handles, add a one-time boot guard, disconnect/clear on pagehide or before rebootstrap, pause periodic refresh while hidden, and prefer event-driven refresh with a slower health-check fallback.
findings.later_target: Remove MutationObserver once the base workspace exposes a stable renderer event contract.

findings.title: CHATGPT_DOCUMENT_AND_SEND_VERIFICATION_USE_TIGHT_BOUNDED_POLLING

evidence.fact: Document readiness executes JavaScript every 500 ms for up to 30 seconds.
Inside the renderer, send-control polling runs every 200 ms up to 10 seconds and user-message verification every 250 ms up to 12 seconds.
Dispatch retries up to five attempts, reloads the webContents and waits 1 second after definitely-not-sent failures.

findings.assessment: The loops are bounded and avoid unbounded retry, but their frequencies are aggressive. One attempt can perform up to roughly 60 main-to-renderer readiness evaluations, then a renderer-side 200/250 ms polling sequence; five retries can multiply this work across multiple hidden role windows.
findings.immediate_target: A6 should record executeJavaScript count, polling duration, reload count and CPU for success, slow-load, missing-input and timeout cases. Replace fixed-frequency polling with did-finish-load/DOM observer signals plus capped adaptive backoff where practical.
findings.later_target: Move prompt readiness and dispatch proof into a dedicated preload bridge with explicit event/ack semantics.

findings.title: C_MODE_RUNTIME_INTERVAL_IS_GUARDED_AND_CLEARED_BUT_RESTART_TIMEOUT_IS_UNTRACKED

evidence.fact: pollIntervalMs is clamped to 5 seconds through 300 seconds; timer and tickInFlight state are explicit.
ensureTimer prevents duplicate intervals and stopTimerIfIdle clears and nulls the interval.
restoreAfterRestart creates an untracked 1.5-second setTimeout tick in addition to ensuring the interval.

findings.assessment: The main interval lifecycle is rational and not a leak. The remaining race is a pending restore timeout firing after a rapid stop/pause unless tick itself rejects the inactive state.
findings.immediate_target: Track and cancel the restore timeout or guard the callback with a generation token; include rapid restore-then-stop in A6 tests.
findings.later_target: Consolidate immediate and periodic ticks under one scheduler abstraction.

findings.title: BASE_YOLLA_WORKER_SHELL_REBUILDS_LARGE_DOM_REGIONS_AND_IGNORES_UNSUBSCRIBE_HANDLES

evidence.fact: Group tabs, role list and cycle event list are rebuilt with innerHTML; render fans out to all render functions.
Registry refresh and role/group selection call full render.
bootstrap attaches DOM events and three IPC subscriptions; returned unsubscribe functions are not retained.
subscribe returns a removeListener closure for each IPC subscription.

findings.assessment: A single renderer lifetime is likely stable, but repeated bootstrap in one document would accumulate DOM and IPC listeners. Full innerHTML replacement also causes avoidable DOM churn on workspace-state events.
findings.immediate_target: Add a boot guard and teardown registry; retain unsubscribe closures; update selected-role/status nodes incrementally when registry structure is unchanged.
findings.later_target: Adopt keyed DOM reconciliation for group/role collections only if A4/A6 show meaningful render cost.

findings.title: ACTIVE_5_10_2_3_7_BROWSERVIEW_LIFECYCLE_HAS_AUTHORITY_EVIDENCE_BUT_NOT_DIRECT_SOURCE_BYTES

evidence.fact: Active authority identifies worker and analysis persistent partitions and main.js as browser/session/window plumbing.

The candidate patch targets ensureBrowserView(WORKER/ANALYSIS), detaches the workspace BrowserView, destroys surviving view webContents on workspace close, nulls view references, and reattaches the selected browser on focus.

findings.assessment: The authority chain proves BrowserView lifecycle exists in the active baseline and includes a close-path destroy strategy, but exact active main.js bytes were not available in this execution environment. No direct active-source leak claim is made.
findings.immediate_target: A6 must count BrowserView/webContents before and after workspace close/reopen and mode/group switching. A3 or the PC Agent should later publish the exact active main.js source bytes or a source package pointer for line-complete follow-up audit.
findings.later_target: Use one attached BrowserView at a time and explicitly destroy deprecated A/E views after successful C-only migration.

negative_findings.window_open_policy: setWindowOpenHandler denies child-window creation and redirects approved navigation/external URLs.
negative_findings.reason: The source contains explicit closed/render-process-gone cleanup, releaseRole transitions, interval guards and bounded retry/timeouts. The audit identifies optimization and measurement targets rather than falsely declaring a static leak.

immediate_targets: Measure per-role hidden BrowserWindow cost with backgroundThrottling=false.
Instrument role-window release latency and verify Map/webContents/process return to baseline.
Track and teardown renderer interval, MutationObserver and IPC subscriptions.
Reduce or adapt 500/200/250 ms polling based on measured CPU and dispatch latency.
Reduce full DOM rebuilds on selection/state-only updates.
later_targets: Event/ack preload bridge for ChatGPT readiness and dispatch proof.
Bounded BrowserWindow pool if A6 proves per-role retention is expensive.
Stable base-workspace render event contract so MutationObserver can be removed.
Publish exact active 5.10.2.3.7 source package for complete line-level follow-up audit.

required_scenarios.action: Keep workspace visible and hidden for equal idle windows; capture 5-second UI refresh and C runtime timer activity.
Create/dispatch 1, 5 and 10 role windows; measure incremental CPU/RAM/process/webContents.
Trigger every releaseRole reason and sample immediately, 5 s, 30 s and 60 s after release.
Repeat same-role and distinct-role open/close/release cycles for at least three equal batches.
Exercise normal, slow-load, missing-input and timeout dispatch; count executeJavaScript/reload/poll iterations.
Burst C-mode/repeat/workspace events and DOM mutations; count rAF renders, refreshes and observer callbacks.
Restore then stop within 1.5 seconds; verify no post-stop tick or timer remains.
Close/reopen workspace and switch modes/groups; verify BrowserView/webContents/listener counts return to baseline.

acceptance_indicators: After explicit release or close grace, live BrowserWindow/webContents/process counts return to the corresponding baseline.
Three equal repeat batches show no monotonic retained-process, listener, Map-entry or memory growth.
Exactly one renderer refresh interval, MutationObserver and subscription set exists per document lifetime.
No renderer polling continues after pagehide/unload or workspace destruction.
C runtime timer_active becomes false at idle/stop and no delayed restore tick mutates stopped state.
Measured polling cost is bounded by source limits and does not produce concurrent poll loops for the same role.
